title: PHANGS-JWST First Results: Interstellar Medium Structure on the Turbulent Jeans Scale in Four Disk Galaxies Observed by JWST and the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array
question: Examine whether the multi-scale network of filamentary features in four nearby disk galaxies observed with JWST/MIRI is consistent with the fragmentation of the gas disk through gravitational instability on the Toomre, turbulent Jeans, or disk scale height scales.

data.angular_resolution: 150 pc-scale (12m+7m+tp for NGC 628, NGC 1365, NGC 7496); convolved to 1.5 kpc resolution (7m+tp for IC 5332)

what.value: Galaxy properties (Distance, inclination, PA, stellar mass, SFR) for the four target galaxies

evidence.quote: Table [\[tab:props\]](#tab:props) lists a number of relevant properties for the four target galaxies (cite: LEE_PHANGSJWST).

what.value: Rotation curves measured from the CO velocity field and analytical fits for NGC 628, NGC 1365, and NGC 7496

evidence.quote: For NGC 628, NGC 1365, and NGC 7496, we adopt the rotation curve measured from the CO velocity field by (cite: lang20) as our estimate of the circular velocity $V_c$.

evidence.loc: Estimating the Turbulent Jeans Length and the Toomre Length
evidence.quote: derived from an analytical fit to the observed rotation curve (cite: lang20).

what.value: Semi-empirical rotation curve model implied by stellar mass and integrated atomic gas mass estimate for IC 5332

evidence.quote: For IC 5332, we use the semi-empirical rotation curve model implied by this galaxy’s stellar mass (cite: leroy21b), following (cite: meidt18).
The integrated mass of atomic gas then equals value estimated for this galaxy (cite: leroy21b).

what.value: PHANGS mega-tables: 1-kpc hexagonal aperture molecular gas surface densities, 150-pc scale molecular gas velocity dispersions, stellar mass surface densities, and resolved HI observations for NGC 628

evidence.quote: For the gas properties (velocity dispersion and surface density), where possible we adopt the values tabulated for the molecular gas in the PHANGS mega-tables recently presented by (cite: sun22).

As our fiducial estimate of the molecular gas velocity dispersion in each aperture, we choose the average velocity dispersion measured specifically on 150 pc scales from the 12m+7m+tp CO(2-1) cubes for NGC 628, NGC 1365 and NGC 7496 (cite: sun22).
In NGC 628, the azimuthally-averaged molecular gas mass fraction is $>$70% over the MIRI field of view using the atomic gas traced by resolved HI observations available for NGC 628 (cite: sun22).

what.value: Stellar scale height z_0 assigned to each galaxy from an empirical scaling relation between z_0 and disk scale length

evidence.quote: Supplementing this set of measured gas properties, in each hexagonal 1-kpc mega-table aperture we also use the tabulated stellar mass surface density and the stellar scale height $z_0$ assigned uniquely to each galaxy according to an empirical scaling relation between $z_0$ and disk scale length (cite: sun20).

what.value: Catalog of bubble candidates in NGC 628 morphologically identified in MIRI images

evidence.quote: Consistent with this expectation, the catalog of bubble candidates in NGC 628 morphologically identified in the MIRI images and visually matched with a stellar counterpart (cite: WATKINS_PHANGSJWST) have average radii 20-30 pc, just at the scale height estimated here (see Figure [3](#fig:spacings)), although they can reach as large as 550 pc.

recipe.goal: Extract gas dynamical properties, surface densities, and velocity dispersions from PHANGS-ALMA CO(2-1) and mega-tables
recipe.method: Adopt rotation curves from CO velocity fields (NGC 628, NGC 1365, NGC 7496) or stellar-mass semi-empirical model (IC 5332) and interpolate onto the JWST map grid. Adopt 1-kpc hexagonal aperture molecular gas surface densities and 150-pc cloud-scale velocity dispersions from PHANGS mega-tables (12m+7m+tp for NGC 628, NGC 1365, NGC 7496). For IC 5332, convolve the 7m+tp moment-0 map to 1.5 kpc resolution, sample at hex centers, apply alpha_CO, and adopt a global minimum velocity dispersion of 1.25 km/s (plus an optional exponential atomic gas component).
key_parameters: 1-kpc hexagonal apertures; 150 pc scale for moment-0 and velocity dispersion (NGC 628, NGC 1365, NGC 7496)
1.5 kpc resolution convolved 7m+tp moment-0 map and minimum velocity dispersion sigma = 1.25 km s^-1 for IC 5332
assumptions: Aperture-dependent alpha_CO following Sun et al. (2022)
Principal fragmentation happens at/near the cloud scale (150 pc)
Optional atomic gas in IC 5332: exponential decline from maximum 10 M_sun pc^-2 with 3.6 kpc scale length and sigma = 7 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Identify filamentary networks in JWST/MIRI F1130W images
recipe.method: Create unsharp mask versions of the MIRI F1130W images by subtracting a Gaussian-smoothed version (sigma = 1.1" or 10 pixels) from the native image, then run FilFinder with global intensity thresholds and minimum width and length cuts to generate filament masks.
key_parameters: Unsharp mask Gaussian smoothing sigma = 1.1" (10 image pixels)
Minimum filament width = 50 pc; minimum filament length = 100 pc (NGC 628, IC 5332) or 500 pc (NGC 1365, NGC 7496)
Unsharp mask global intensity threshold = 0.03 MJy/sr (NGC 628, IC 5332, NGC 7496) or 0.2 MJy/sr (NGC 1365)
assumptions: Shorter or narrower lower-intensity elongated structures do not contribute to the main filamentary web and originate from a different mechanism

recipe.goal: Measure characteristic azimuthal and radial spacings between filaments
recipe.method: For NGC 628 and IC 5332, divide FilFinder masks into narrow elliptical annuli (width = 3 pixels or 1 resolution element) at the galaxy's inclination and PA, find intersections with >= 5 pixels, compute nearest-neighbor azimuthal separations in each ring, and average over 20 radial bins (300 pc-wide annuli). For NGC 1365 and NGC 7496, divide masks into 1-degree wide azimuthal segments, find radial intersections with >= 5 pixels, and calculate mean and standard deviation of nearest-neighbor radial separations in two radial zones (R < 2.5 kpc and R > 2.5 kpc) across azimuths away from bar ends.
key_parameters: Annulus width = 1 resolution element (3 pixels, 15 pc at NGC 628); radial averaging over 20 bins (300 pc-wide annuli); intersection threshold N_pix = 5 pixels
Azimuthal segment width = 1 degree; radial zones R < 2.5 kpc and R > 2.5 kpc; intersection threshold N_pix = 5 pixels
assumptions: Galaxy inclination and position angle from Table 1 used to project elliptical annuli

recipe.goal: Calculate Toomre length, 2D most unstable wavelength, Toomre Q, gas scale height, and 3D turbulent Jeans length, and compare with filament spacings
recipe.method: In each 1-kpc hexagonal aperture, compute epicyclic frequency kappa from analytical rotation curve fits, Toomre length lambda_T = 4*pi^2*G*Sigma/kappa^2, 2D most unstable wavelength lambda_2D = 2*sigma^2/(G*Sigma), and Toomre Q. Estimate vertical gas scale height h either by assuming a fixed h = 100 pc or by solving the quadratic hydrostatic equilibrium equation with gas self-gravity and background stellar density rho_b, then compute mid-plane gas density rho = Sigma/(sqrt(2*pi)*h) and 3D turbulent Jeans length lambda_J = sigma*pi^(1/2)/(G*rho)^(1/2). Compare radial profiles of these scales against measured filament spacings.
key_parameters: Fixed gas scale height h = 100 pc (for Table 1 values) or hydrostatic equilibrium h (typically 30 to 100 pc)
assumptions: Gas is isothermal and follows a Gaussian vertical distribution rho propto exp(-z^2/(2h^2)) such that Sigma = rho*sqrt(2*pi)*h
Background gravitational potential is dominated by the stellar distribution, omitting atomic gas and dark matter halo (unless specified for IC 5332)

score_reason: All underlying ALMA data products (PHANGS-ALMA moment maps and Sun et al. 2022 mega-tables) and JWST/MIRI images are publicly available, and the mathematical equations and primary spatial/intensity thresholds are clearly stated. However, a few secondary FilFinder parameters and the exact azimuthal ranges excluded near the bar ends in NGC 1365 and NGC 7496 are not explicitly specified.
rediscovery_reason: Both the PHANGS-JWST MIRI images and the PHANGS-ALMA mega-tables/moment maps are public, the analytical formulas for Toomre and Jeans lengths are completely specified, and the primary numeric results (Table 1 means and 16th-84th percentile ranges for all four galaxies) provide a clear quantitative benchmark.
